details.description: Claude Haiku 4.5 is Anthropic's fastest model, released October 15, 2025 for low-latency, real-time use at near-frontier intelligence. It takes text and image input, supports manual extended thinking and tool use (including coding, bash, web search, and computer-use tools), and offers a 200K-token context window with a 64K-token max output. Anthropic reports coding performance similar to the earlier Claude Sonnet 4 at about one-third the cost and more than twice the speed, and released it under AI Safety Level 2, its lowest current safety level.
advantages: Scored 73.3% on SWE-bench Verified at launch, per Anthropic's announcement.
Scored 41.75% on Terminal-Bench with thinking enabled, per Anthropic's announcement.
Anthropic reports coding performance similar to Claude Sonnet 4 at about one-third the cost and more than twice the speed.
Anthropic's announcement reports lower rates of misaligned behavior in testing than both Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.1.
disadvantages: Reliable knowledge cutoff of February 2025, the oldest among Anthropic's current models, per Anthropic's model page.
200K-token context window and 64K-token max output, smaller than the 1M-token/128K-token limits on Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.
Uses manual extended thinking (thinking.type: 'enabled' with a token budget) rather than the adaptive thinking on Anthropic's newer flagship models.
use_cases: Low-latency chat assistants and customer service agents
Multi-agent orchestration, running many parallel Haiku sub-agents under a larger coordinating model

notes: Catalog's deprecation_date (2026-10-15) matches Anthropic's own retirement date of 'not sooner than October 15, 2026' exactly. Catalog's 200K input / 64K output token facts and image+text/text modality match Anthropic's model page exactly.
